definition: Locating faces in an image with bounding boxes or landmarks — the front end for recognition, alignment, and tracking.
details: Locating faces in an image with bounding boxes or landmarks — the front end for recognition, alignment, and tracking. Cascades and anchor-based detectors made it a solved, real-time task.

explainer.lead: Face detection finds where faces appear in an image and marks them with boxes or key points called landmarks. It gives later systems a face to work with, making tasks such as recognition, alignment, and tracking possible.

tiers.eli5: Face detection is like drawing a rectangle around every face in a class photo. It does not need to know who anyone is; it just notices, “There is a face here.” Those rectangles can then help a computer line up faces or follow them through a video.
tiers.practitioner: Use face detection as the first stage of a vision pipeline, then pass its bounding boxes or landmarks to recognition, alignment, or tracking components. Cascades and anchor-based detectors support real-time use, but inaccurate boxes or landmarks can degrade every downstream stage.
tiers.paperLevel: Given an image I, face detection predicts a set of face locations, typically bounding boxes b_i and optionally landmark coordinates l_i. It solves localization rather than identification: the output indicates where faces are, not who they belong to.

explainer.example: For a group photo containing three faces, a detector returns three bounding boxes, one around each face. An alignment stage can then crop and position those regions before recognition runs.

usedIn.name: Face recognition pipelines
usedIn.detail: Supplies the image regions that a later recognition stage processes.

usedIn.name: Face alignment
usedIn.detail: Uses detected boxes or landmarks to position faces consistently for subsequent processing.

usedIn.name: Video face tracking
usedIn.detail: Provides face locations that can be followed from frame to frame.

explainer.intuition: Instead of asking who a person is, face detection asks a simpler question: where are the faces? Its output turns a whole image into one or more localized face regions.
howItWorks: Search for patterns that indicate the presence of a face.
Estimate a bounding box around each detected face.
Optionally predict landmarks that mark key face locations.
Pass these locations to recognition, alignment, or tracking.
explainer.whyItMatters: Detection is the front end for many face-processing systems: downstream components need a face location before they can recognize, align, or track it. Cascades and anchor-based detectors made this task practical in real time.
misconceptions: Face detection locates faces; face recognition determines or compares identities.
A bounding box marks a face region, while landmarks mark specific points on the face.
